open_obligations: Do not compare ASD values with Khan et al.'s judge accuracy numbers.
Note that Sudhir et al.'s experiments use only 100 questions, one judge model and five agent models.
Check whether giving agents tools changes the capability ordering.
out.other_title: Self-play debate: judge accuracy rises with debater aggregate rating
out.rationale: Khan et al. report judge accuracy rises with debater aggregate rating in self-play debates with a GPT-4-Turbo judge, as debaters are optimised against win rate (judge preference). Sudhir et al. say they reproduce this with new metrics: in Debate, higher Expected Agent Score goes with higher ASD, in small experiments with 100 questions, one gpt-4o-mini judge model and five agent models, on the GSM8K dataset; the cited passages do not say they optimise agents against judge preference. Judge and metrics also differ, and the cited Khan et al. passage does not name its dataset, so magnitudes are not comparable.
out.scope: proposed SAME_QUESTION_DIFFERENT_SETTING: whether debate's truth-favouring signal strengthens as debaters become more capable

text: The paper reports reproducing Khan et al. (2024) with its new metrics: in Debate, higher Expected Agent Score is associated with higher ASD, which the authors take to suggest Debate will keep incentivizing alignment as capabilities scale, while noting this is not a formal guarantee for the superhuman regime.
title: In Debate, more capable (higher-EAS) agents give higher ASD
